problem.title: At Least One Head
problem.statement: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability of getting at least one head?
hints: List the four ordered coin outcomes.
At least one head excludes only TT.

solutionSteps.title: Build the sample space
solutionSteps.body: The equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH, and TT.

solutionSteps.title: Mark the event
solutionSteps.body: HH, HT, and TH each contain at least one head.

solutionSteps.title: Compare part to whole
solutionSteps.body: Three of the four equally likely outcomes are favorable, so the probability is 3/4.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of HH, HT, TH, TT
notes: Recomputed answer: 3 favorable outcomes among 4 equally likely outcomes gives 3/4.

problem.title: Repeated Spinner Colors
problem.statement: A fair spinner has 6 equal sections colored red, red, red, blue, green, and green. What is the probability of landing on red?
hints: Treat the equal sections as the elementary outcomes.
Count the red sections and all sections.

solutionSteps.title: Choose equal outcomes
solutionSteps.body: The six equal sections are equally likely.

solutionSteps.title: Count red sections
solutionSteps.body: Three of the six sections are red.

validationMethods: direct count of 3 red sections among 6 equal sections
independent symmetry check that red and non-red each occupy 3 sections

problem.title: Matching Coin Faces
problem.statement: Two fair coins are tossed. What is the probability that the two coins show the same face?
hints: Mark the outcomes with identical letters.

solutionSteps.title: List equally likely outcomes
solutionSteps.body: The sample space is HH, HT, TH, TT.

solutionSteps.title: Mark matches
solutionSteps.body: HH and TT show the same face.

solutionSteps.title: Form the ratio
solutionSteps.body: Two of four outcomes match, so 2/4=1/2.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of four ordered outcomes
independent symmetry check: one matching second face for each first face

problem.title: Multiples of Three
problem.statement: One card is chosen at random from cards numbered 1 through 8. What is the probability that its number is a multiple of 3?
hints: Write every card in the sample space.
The multiples of 3 in this range are 3 and 6.

solutionSteps.title: Build the sample space
solutionSteps.body: There are eight equally likely cards numbered 1 through 8.

validationMethods: exhaustive divisibility check of integers 1 through 8
independent count using floor(8/3)=2 favorable cards

problem.title: An Even Spinner Sum
problem.statement: One fair spinner is numbered 1 and 2 in equal sections. Another fair spinner is numbered 1, 2, and 3 in equal sections. Both are spun. What is the probability that the sum is even?
hints: An even sum comes from two odds or two evens.

solutionSteps.title: Build the sample space
solutionSteps.body: The 2 choices and 3 choices form 6 equally likely ordered pairs.

solutionSteps.title: Mark even sums
solutionSteps.body: The pairs (1,1), (1,3), and (2,2) have even sums.

solutionSteps.title: Form the ratio
solutionSteps.body: Three of six pairs are favorable, so 3/6=1/2.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of all six ordered spinner pairs
independent parity count: 1×2 odd-odd pairs plus 1×1 even-even pair
notes: Recomputed answer: 3 favorable pairs among 6 gives 1/2.

problem.title: An Even Spinner Product
problem.statement: One fair spinner is numbered 1, 2, and 3 in equal sections. Another fair spinner is numbered 1, 2, 3, and 4 in equal sections. Both are spun. What is the probability that the product is even?
hints: There are 3×4 equally likely ordered pairs.
A product fails to be even only when both numbers are odd.

solutionSteps.title: Build the sample space
solutionSteps.body: The two spinners create 12 equally likely ordered pairs.

solutionSteps.title: Count odd products
solutionSteps.body: Both results must be odd. Each spinner has 2 odd choices, making 2×2=4 odd-product pairs.

solutionSteps.title: Use the complement
solutionSteps.body: The other 12-4=8 pairs have even products, so the probability is 8/12=2/3.

validationMethods: exhaustive 3-by-4 product parity table with 8 even entries
notes: Recomputed answer: 8/12=2/3; the four odd-odd pairs are (1,1), (1,3), (3,1), and (3,3).
